text:
alex: heads-up — last night's GPU pages were pretty noisy. ~10 pages for short 1–2m flares in worker-pool-us-west. Can we move a bunch of these to tickets instead of waking people?

mira: +1. sounds like we need stricter grouping + a 'sustained' vs 'spike' split. Spikes (OOMs, driver crashes) should page. Sustained high util should ticket.

samir: agree. current alert is just `gpu_utilization > 0.9` with no `for` so any blip pages. propose:
```yaml
alert: GPUHighSustained
expr: avg_over_time(gpu_utilization{pool="worker",region="us-west"}[10m]) > 0.85
for: 15m
labels:
  severity: ticket
```
and keep a paging alert for error spikes: `increase(gpu_oom_total[5m]) > 0` -> severity: pager.

liz: also +1 for grouping by pool+cluster+region so one page for a noisy host doesn't wake entire rotation. e.g. Alertmanager `group_by: ["pool","cluster","region"]`.

chris: + practical note: quiet windows for non-prod pools are fine, but for prod we should avoid blanket mutes. maybe allow `mute` for non-prod in 02:00–05:00 and rely on ticketing for sustained stuff.

alex: concrete thresholds we discussed: paging if `rate(gpu_oom_total[5m]) > 0` OR `gpu_temp > 95` OR `instance_down == 1` — immediate page. Ticket if `avg_over_time(gpu_utilization[10m]) > 0.85` OR `p95_latency_inference > 500ms` for 20m.

mira: can we express p95-based condition? e.g.:
```promql
quantile_over_time(0.95, model_infer_latency_seconds_bucket{job="inference"}[15m]) > 0.5
```
If true for 15m -> ticket.

samir: alertmanager routing rule idea: use label `pager: "true"` vs `pager: "false"` derived from `severity` and `urgency`. oncall-bot can honor that and only page when `pager: "true"`.

oncall-bot: I can route based on label. To enable: add `pager: "true"` to alerts that should page and update routing tree. I will not auto-mute any pager labeled alerts.

liz: we should also add flapping suppression: `for` + `resend` rules and a 30m dedupe window for the same `group_key` to avoid repeated pages.

chris: ops playbook updates: 1) update alerts in prometheus/grafana repo, 2) add grouping labels in exporter (gpu host -> pool/cluster), 3) update alertmanager route. I'll own 1 and 2. samir can own route changes.

amended alert yaml examples for the repo: 
```yaml
- alert: GPUOOMSpike
  expr: increase(gpu_oom_total{pool="worker"}[5m]) > 0
  for: 0m
  labels:
    severity: page
    pager: "true"

- alert: GPUHighSustained
  expr: avg_over_time(gpu_utilization{pool="worker"}[10m]) > 0.85
  for: 15m
  labels:
    severity: ticket
    pager: "false"
```

alex: can we also add a performance dashboard panel with `alerts by group` so SREs and platform owners can tune thresholds per-cluster? helps avoid one-size-fits-all.

mira: yep — add a grafana panel using: `count by (alertname, pool, cluster) (ALERTS{state="firing"})` and a heatmap over last 7d.

samir: follow-ups: I'll open a PR with the alert changes + route update, chris will add grouping labels exporter-side, liz will update runbook (what pages mean vs tickets). target: PRs by EOW.

alex: perfect. once PRs land we'll run a 2-week canary: convert 50% of worker-pool-us-west alerts to ticket severity and monitor SLO error budget and paging volume. if pages drop and SLO stable -> roll out.

liz: noted. I'll add a Grafana panel for page vs ticket counts and a slack webhook to #eng-sre for ticket-only spikes so product owners can triage.

chris: one more: cost note — sustained high GPU util -> consider autoscale rules before alerting to ticket. cheaper to scale than to page. add autoscale triggers: `avg_over_time(gpu_utilization[10m]) > 0.9` -> scale up.

alex: thanks all. action items tracked in PRs and a short retro after canary. :thumbsup:
